entry: Cacheable and CacheEvict Flux through the managed retry proxy

questions.history: Call the retryable cacheable method on a miss.
questions.prediction: The PR reports a parent hang on retry. The landing should complete with [a,b], reach the source twice and cache the list [a,b].
questions.basis: The fixture succeeds on the second subscription. The no-argument method uses SimpleKey.EMPTY, so a separate cache read can confirm publication.
questions.refutation: The retry never reaches the source again, times out, delivers different values, or leaves the key absent.

fix.return: values=[a, b] terminal=complete subscriptions=2 cache=[a, b]

questions.history: Have the very first subscription succeed with [a,b]. Call the same proxy method again after completion.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should deliver [a,b] twice, with one source subscription in total.
questions.basis: A successful cached sequence is replayable under the same key without running its producer.
questions.refutation: A successful first call fails to populate the cache or the repeat subscribes to the source again.

parent.return: first=[a, b] second=[a, b] subscriptions=1 cache=[a, b]

fix.return: first=[a, b] second=[a, b] subscriptions=1 cache=[a, b]

questions.history: Use @CacheEvict("tests") in place of @Cacheable. Preload SimpleKey.EMPTY with [old] and retain the error-then-success source.
questions.prediction: The parent is expected to stall at retry. On the landing, the caller should receive [a,b] and the independent cache lookup should be empty after completion.
questions.basis: Eviction after a successful invocation removes the existing key. The return sequence and cache state can disagree.
questions.refutation: The Flux stalls or succeeds while the sentinel entry survives.

questions.history: On a fresh cacheable miss, make the failed first attempt emit "partial" before its IOException. The successful retry still emits [a,b].
questions.prediction: On the landing the continuous downstream collector should see [partial,a,b]. The stored list and a subsequent cache-hit call should each yield only [a,b], with the source count still two.
questions.basis: Reactive retry resubscribes after already delivered values. Only the successfully completed attempt qualifies to populate this cache entry.
questions.refutation: The consumer loses its already delivered prefix, or a later cache hit replays a value from the failed attempt.

fix.return: values=[partial, a, b] terminal=complete subscriptions=2 cache=[a, b] hit=[a, b] finalSubscriptions=2
